Result: exactly 1 commission (status accrued, $5 = 20% of $25) and 1 driver_payout (pending, $20 = gross - commission). No new 'owed' entry. Account deletion: API (wrong password 400, success, then /me 401, login 401/403, PII anonymized) and UI (logged out it shows instructions only with no button; logged in the button stays disabled until the password is entered and 'DELETE' typed exactly; after deleting it goes to '/' with the token cleared, and logging in again gets 401). critical.issue: CVOR comes back required:true with the old description ('Required for operating commercial motor vehicles in Ontario'). ONTARIO_PERMITS in code was changed to required:False, but startup only seeds db.permits when the collection is empty, so the existing DB row (and production) never gets the change. Add an idempotent startup update: db.permits.update_one({'id':'cvor'}, {'$set': {'required': False, 'description': <new text>}}).

Double-payout risk. The webhook and the /payments/status poll each do find_one(tx not paid), then update, then settle, with no atomic claim. The facility_payments find_one-then-insert check is not atomic either. If both arrive together, both run _transfer_pending_payouts. That function reads the 'pending' payouts and calls stripe.Transfer.create before the conditional update, with no idempotency_key, so the driver can be paid twice. Fix: claim the tx atomically (update_one({session_id, payment_status:{$ne:'paid'}}) and only settle if modified_count==1). Claim each payout atomically (pending to 'transferring') before the transfer. Pass idempotency_key=payout['id'] to Transfer.create. Add a unique index on facility_payments(facility_id, month) for status paid.

critical.endpoint: Facility statement settlement vs legacy 'owed' commissions
critical.issue: Reproduced in the DB. 5 demo.driver jobs delivered this month under the old model have commission status 'owed' and no driver_payout row. The facility paid the full $254.25 statement covering them (facility_paid:true), yet the driver still owes $25 (Pay $25.00 Now is shown) and gets $0 payout for those trips. In production, any jobs delivered before cut-over in an unpaid month would charge the driver twice. Fix: on facility_statement settlement, for jobs that have a legacy 'owed' commission, mark it paid/waived and create the missing driver_payout (gross - commission). Or migrate the current month's 'owed' rows to 'accrued' plus a payout.

minor.issue: Every click creates a new Checkout session; there are now 5 unpaid sessions open for 2026-11 for the same facility. If a facility completes a second one (another tab, back button), Stripe charges them, but _settle_ledger_for_session returns early ('idempotent') and nothing is recorded or refunded: a silent double charge. Reuse or expire the existing open session (stripe.checkout.Session.expire), and in settlement flag/refund a second paid session.

Paying mid-month marks the month as paid permanently. Jobs delivered later in the same month show in the statement (total grows), but pay returns 400 'already paid'. Those jobs never get facility_paid, their commission stays accrued forever, and the driver payout is never released. Store paid job_ids with the payment and allow paying the unpaid remainder (or bill only closed months).

The statement includes jobs by posted_by OR facility_id in all owned facilities. Settlement only flags jobs with facility_id == the first facility found. Jobs posted without a facility_id, or under a second owned facility, are billed but never marked facility_paid, so their payouts never release.
The driver_payout insert has no unique index (the commission one is unique on job_id+type). Add a partial unique index for type 'driver_payout' as a backstop.
Checkout showed USD $184.33 preselected, with CA$254.25 as an alternative (Stripe adaptive pricing on the account). Facilities may pay in USD. Consider disabling adaptive pricing for CAD invoices.

ui_bugs.issue: No in-app link to /delete-account anywhere (no nav/profile/settings entry; the only reference is text on the Privacy page). The Privacy page says 'can also be requested from your profile in the app', which isn't true. Apple 5.1.1(v) requires deletion to be easy to find in the app. Add a 'Delete account' link in the driver/facility/dispatcher headers or account menu.

integration_issues.issue: Polling stops after 8 attempts (about 16s) and silently resets the URL if the payment isn't 'paid' yet (slow webhook or bank delay). The user gets no 'payment processing' message. Also after returning, the default tab is Book & Track, not Billing.

HIGH: Add a visible in-app 'Delete account' entry point linking to /delete-account for driver/facility/dispatcher. Fix the Privacy wording if needed.
Expire or reuse open checkout sessions per facility+month, and detect/refund a second paid session.
Allow paying the unpaid remainder of a month (or bill only closed months) so jobs delivered after a mid-month payment are not stranded.

Update the driver Billing page copy for the payout model.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 4,922 lines; billing/payments/payouts should be in their own router module.
_transfer_pending_payouts calls stripe.Transfer.create without an idempotency_key, and updates status only after the transfer succeeds.
Webhook and status poll both use non-atomic read-then-write on payment_transactions (this affects tips and balance too).
facility_billing paid detection uses find_one(owner_user_id), so it only checks the first facility when a user owns several.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the requested UI flows work (1 HIGH discoverability gap)

rca of the issue: CVOR: startup seeds db.permits only when count==0, so code changes to ONTARIO_PERMITS never reach an existing DB.
